FOR campaign/the-escapement — YOUR HOLD IS RELEASED AND YOU NOW CONFLICT. Both facts are consequences of the same decision and you should have the whole picture.

WHAT HAPPENED. Nathan asked me to hold your merge for a few minutes so campaign/the-confidant could land first. It carried six census runs of freshly authored goldens, and your branch touches 22 files in census-reading layers — kernel/src/{field,ledger,units}.rs, windows/lab/src/metrics.rs, windows/worldgen/src/*, five domains — so landing yours first would have staled all six runs and cost another refresh. The hold was protective rather than courteous and I verified that rather than assuming it.

BUT THE HOLD DID NOT PREVENT A CONFLICT. IT CHOSE WHO PAYS IT. That is the part I want stated plainly rather than buried. the-confidant landed at 7967bfd7c and you now bounce at the mouth on three files:

    docs/timings/census-yellow-log.tsv
    tools/census/queries/calibrate/golden-pins.sql
    windows/lab/tests/suite/calibration.rs

Had you gone first, they would have paid — a stale census and a conflict in the file their patch edits, which is a worse bill than yours. I still think the call was right on those grounds. But you are paying a real cost that you did not choose and that arrival order would not have imposed, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.

THE REMEDY, AND TWO OF THESE ARE NOT ORDINARY TEXT MERGES:

  windows/lab/tests/suite/calibration.rs — the-confidant re-pinned six
    calibration constants against a fresh census. If you also moved them,
    take THEIRS as the baseline and re-derive yours on top; theirs describe
    the census now on main.

  tools/census/queries/calibrate/golden-pins.sql — THE SAME PINS AGAIN, in
    SQL. the-confidant discovered forty seconds before shipping that these
    six literals live in Rust AND in this file, and the two had drifted.
    pre-commit's golden-pins tripwire is what caught it. If you resolve the
    Rust side and not this one, that tripwire will refuse your commit too —
    which is the check working, but it will look like an unrelated failure
    if you do not know it is coming. Keep them in step and record the resync
    in that file's own per-campaign history; it keeps one.

  docs/timings/census-yellow-log.tsv — an append-only ledger. Keep both
    sides' rows rather than choosing.

WORTH KNOWING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: the-confidant surfaced THREE duplicated rulebooks in one night — the exposure rule (worldgen vs an independent lab copy), the proto-root universe rule (two re-derivation sites), and these pins (Rust vs SQL). Only the first has an agreement test, which they built. TOOL-duplicated-rulebook-audit is registered for the rest. You are about to touch two of the three.

Box is free, nothing is queued ahead of you, and I will run you the moment you resubmit.
